nonLabourLines.description: Legacy data migration tooling & Oracle export licensing
Contingency buffer for third-party API changes

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; hour estimates are derived from story points and task complexity, not past performance, and should be revisited once early sprints provide real velocity data.
1 story point ≈ 6-7 hours of blended effort, adjusted per task based on described complexity (e.g. RBAC and data migration carry extra integration/testing overhead).

DevOps Engineer is only 0.4 FTE (~16 hrs/week); allocated hours (90) are concentrated on CI/staging setup (PW-1) and light support during Stripe/migration cutover — this role is staffed thinly relative to the infrastructure-heavy backlog (PW-1, PW-7, PW-8) and is a scheduling risk.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE (~24 hrs/week) is assumed to test all 8 backlog items; given the volume, QA effort is concentrated on Urgent/High priority items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration) with lighter coverage on Medium items.
Backend Developer effort (1.5 FTE) dominates hours because 5 of 8 backlog items (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, CI) are backend/infra heavy.
Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) covers the design system, dashboard, invoice UI, and RBAC UI enforcement.

Legacy data migration (PW-8, 21 points) is treated as the highest-effort task and assumes a phased migration with parallel validation rather than a single cutover; actual effort could vary significantly depending on legacy schema quality, which is not yet known.
Payment provider integration (PW-7) assumes standard Stripe Checkout/Elements plus webhooks; deeper PCI scope (e.g., custom card fields) would increase cost.
Non-labour costs cover Stripe/PCI review, migration tooling and Oracle export licensing, initial staging/CI cloud infrastructure, and a contingency line for third-party API changes.
Estimate assumes a single delivery team with no parallel workstream duplication, and no allowance for scope changes beyond the listed backlog.
P75 and P90 scenarios add contingency for backend/QA schedule slippage (given DevOps is thinly staffed) and legacy migration data-quality unknowns.
input.reasoning: Hours were built bottom-up from story points (~6-7 hrs/point blended) then adjusted per task: CI/staging (PW-1) leans DevOps+Backend; design system (PW-2) and dashboard/invoice UI (PW-5, PW-6) lean Frontend; auth (PW-3) and RBAC (PW-4) split Backend/Frontend with QA emphasis; payments (PW-7) is Backend+QA heavy given webhook/reconciliation complexity; legacy migration (PW-8) is the largest single cost driver, dominated by Backend hours plus QA validation, with DevOps support for cutover. Role hours were checked against each role's FTE capacity (e.g., DevOps 0.4 FTE, QA 0.6 FTE) to avoid overloading thinly-staffed roles beyond what's plausible in a normal delivery timeframe (~3-4 months), which surfaced DevOps as a likely bottleneck. The P50 scenario equals the sum of labour and non-labour lines exactly (129,264.60 USD). P75 and P90 layer on contingency (~10% and ~22% respectively) for schedule risk from thin DevOps staffing, QA bandwidth constraints, and unknowns in the legacy Oracle migration and Stripe PCI scope.

reductions.description: Descope Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) to a later phase, delivering the portal for new customers first and migrating historical records in a follow-up project.
reductions.effect: Removes the largest single cost driver (21 points); reduces Backend, QA and DevOps hours tied to migration validation and cutover.

reductions.description: Reduce Design System scope (PW-2) to only the components actually needed for PW-3 through PW-6 (buttons, forms, tables) and defer full theming/dialog polish.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~65 Frontend Developer hours by narrowing component library scope to MVP needs.

reductions.description: Use a Stripe-hosted Checkout page instead of custom Elements integration for Payment Provider Integration (PW-7), reducing custom UI and PCI scope.
reductions.effect: Cuts Frontend and Backend hours on PW-7 and lowers the Stripe/PCI compliance review non-labour cost.

reductions.description: Defer non-essential staging/CI cloud infrastructure spend (multi-environment redundancy) until post-launch; keep a single staging slot as scoped in PW-1.
reductions.effect: Halves the staging/CI cloud infrastructure non-labour line by deferring redundant environments.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) by relying on developer self-testing and automated checks, reserving dedicated QA Engineer time for Urgent/High priority items.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 QA Engineer hours from Medium-priority backlog items.
